div.p: Multi-temporal differential synthetic aperture radar interferometry techniques are well-developed and beneficial tools for deformation analysis using remotely sensed images. The primary objective of the study is to investigate the capability and the performance of the new generation SAR system Sentinel-1 data to detect and monitor surface deformation. We combined open source tools of Sentinel Application Platform (SNAP) and Stanford Method for Persistent Scatterers (StaMPS) for data processing. The results highlight the recent surface displacement rates over the Istanbul city. The deformation rates reach up to approximately 8 mm/yr over a 4 year period.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Highly urbanized cities play an important role within the socio-economic structure of the countries. Meanwhile, they are very vulnerable due to rapid increase of the population. In addition to natural hazards, cities and infrastructure of it are under risk of anthropogenic-related damages. The detection and continuous monitoring of surface deformation is a key factor to prevent possible risks and sustainable development of the urban planning. In this context, satellite based Synthetic Aperture RADAR (SAR) data and Differential SAR Interferometry (DInSAR) technique provide a powerful tool for remote detection of surface displacement, mapping and long term monitoring of several phenomena [1]. Particularly, advanced multi-temporal DInSAR approaches known as Persistent Scatterer Interferometry (PSI) [2] [3] and Small Baseline Subset (SBAS) [3][4] are capable of determining spatial deformation pattern in both local and regional scales. Both approaches have been successfully applied for several geophysical phenomena such as landslides [5][6], subsidence [7][8] and seismic events [9] [10].

Previous studies using different data, time span and InSAR techniques have showed the deformation rate and its evolution in time over Istanbul. A mean ground velocity map over Istanbul using ERS and Envisat dataset from 1992 to 2010 has been presented by [11]. The result indicates subsidence pattern at urbanized areas especially at the west site of the region. The crustal deformation near Istanbul was analyzed using ERS and Envisat data [12]. The SBAS results of multi-looked dataset present approximately 5 mm/yr at Line of Sight (LOS) direction. A detailed analysis was conducted using SBAS technique with TerraSAR-X data and it concluded that there were local deformation patterns over the city center of Istanbul [13]. Within the one and half year time span (Nov 2010-Jun 2011) mean deformation velocity values have reached up to approximately 3-4 cm movements away from the satellite at LOS direction. Most of the deformation occurred at places where man-made filled recreation areas were located [13]. Detection of deformation and continuous monitoring of the city is crucial for risk management and sustainable planning of the city. To this aim, current surface deformation over settlement, recreation areas and transportation network were under investigation from 2014 to 2017. New generation SAR missions of Sentinel-1A/B satellites images which are free-of-charge and cover large areas were utilized. PSI method was applied due to lack of limitation by baseline decorrelation and being a suitable method for long term analysis in urbanized regions [14]. This paper addresses capability of Sentinel-1 data for deformation analysis on densely urbanized megacity Istanbul using StaMPS method [3]. The remaining sections of this paper are organized as follows. Section 2 outlines details of materials and methodology used. Up to date deformation pattern and velocity maps are presented in Section 3. And finally, Section 4 summarizes the outcome of this paper and explains planned future works.

div.head: Study Area: İstanbul
div.p: The study area Istanbul is located in the north-west of Turkey, Figure 1. The Marmara Sea and the Black Sea lie on the south and north of Istanbul, respectively. Rapid urbanization has had a drastic impact on the urban sprawl of the city. Both natural and man-induced hazards have played a role in deformation formation. As a megacity, it has more than 15 million inhabitants which cause major land use changes affecting ecology. Additionally, the city is located on North Anatolian Fault which is the cause of major earthquakes. In this work, we focus on the Golden Horn and the Historical Peninsula to be able to compare produced results with previously reported analysis [13].

div.head: Sentinel-1 Data
div.p: Sentinel-1 is one of Sentinels mission satellites which provide radar imaging all-weather, day-and-night for land and ocean services at C-band under Copernicus programme. We utilize 123 Sentinel-1 SAR data at ascending orbit acquired in TOPSAR Interferometric Wide (IW) Swath Mode in Single Look Complex (SLC) format for orbit number 58 and 114 Sentinel-1 descending IW SLC data for orbit number 36. For both ascending and descending datasets VV polarization bands are processed. The data covers the time period between October 2014 and October 2017. The dataset consists of both Sentinel-1A for the whole time period and Sentinel-1B missions starting from October 2016. The single master image is selected based on the geometrical and temporal baseline of the Sentinel-1 A/B images (Figure 2). Master images, 30 th of July 2016 for ascending dataset and 29 th of July for descending datasets, are selected from summer time period in which atmospheric conditions are considered to be less disturbing to interferometric phase compared to other time periods of the year.

div.head: Multi-Temporal InSAR Processing
div.p: There are two main processing blocks for time series analysis of InSAR data [14].The first part of the analysis which includes interferogram formation of all data and removing topographic phase steps are accomplished using Sentinel Application Platform (SNAP, version 6.0 Prev5) [15]. SNAP is the common architecture of scientific exploitation of Sentinel 1/2/3 missions and one of the lead software that supports interferometric processing of Sentinel family of PSI methods which exploit specific single scatterer and allow very high-resolution monitoring [3]. Details of processing steps of StaMPS algorithms are provided in the right part of Figure 3. All formed interferograms are controlled and the ones that have high standard deviation or shows strong atmospheric effect are eliminated from PSI processing (red circles that had no connection to others in Figure 2). In the first part, persistent scatterer (PS) candidates are selected. Then for each PS candidate spatially correlated phase is found and subtracted. At the end, 3D phase unwrapping is applied and error estimation is done. StaMPS processing parameters are tuned for reasonable mitigation of errors.

div.head: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
div.p: A deformation velocity map was produced with the application of PSI technique over the previously specified region of Istanbul. For both ascending and descending datasets mean velocities are shown in Figure 4 with a common interval of ±8 mm/year. Surface displacement is measured along the line of sight (LOS) of the satellite since SAR sensors can only measure the projection of the real movement along the LOS direction. Negative values (red colors) mean displacement occurred away from the satellite and positive values (blue colors) means displacement towards the satellite. White star shows the reference point for measurements considered to be stable over the period. Deformation velocity maps reveal that there are several areas affected by subsidence phenomenon mostly located along the coastal zones of the Golden Horn and human interventions areas that changed the landscape. We want to emphasize three specific sub-regions shown as white rectangles in Figure 4 to discuss our preliminary results for deformation phenomenon.

Region 1 which is located around the area called Miniaturk shows similar deformation pattern for both ascending and descending analysis meaning vertical displacement. Similar deformation pattern for the same area is reported between 2010 and 2012 in [13]. Deformation velocity maps obtained in this work show us that the subsidence phenomenon at the same area continued between 2014 and 2017. The Second region is around the Sirkeci Marmaray station and in [13] it is reported that the area is affected by significant deformation rates. After inspecting the same area in Figure 4, it would not be wrong to say that although deformation still continues, the strength of the deformation rate has slowed down. Ground conditions of the railway station and the neighborhood should be investigated in more details supporting with additional deformation measurements. The third region that is called Yenikapı Activity Area is constructed between 2012 and 2014 as the recreation area for festivals, activities and social rally.

Although both ascending and descending datasets indicate similar deformation pattern, descending deformation map shows more extensive LOS deformation at almost every point of the activity area of shores than ascending one. Difference deformation pattern between ascending and descending datasets is an indication of horizontal deformation.

div.head: CONCLUSION AND FUTURE WORKS
div.p: In this paper, the temporal behavior of land deformations in sub-region of Istanbul is analyzed by applying PSI technique to the Sentinel-1 A/B datasets from 2014 to 2017. Produced deformation velocity maps for both ascending and descending datasets show that certain regions of the city are exposed to subsidence over the years. Preliminary results obtained in this work need to be validated through other surface deformation methods like GPS measurements. Moreover, in order to increase measurement accuracy atmospheric effect should also be removed from each slave images. Besides that, LOS deformation obtained from ascending and descending datasets should be combined to obtain real vertical and horizontal displacements. This study is the first step of a broader project: continuous deformation monitoring of Istanbul City using SAR and GPS data. Continuous monitoring of deformation is crucial for risk management and sustainable planning of the city. The outcomes of this work suggest that the PSI technique can have a high potential in the field of near-real time land deformation monitoring using Sentinel-1 data. To achieve this goal, we will implement fully parallelized version of PSI that is capable of working on multiple processor stations and computer clusters.
